content: 1. Administer 2.5 g of the drug intravenously every 6 hours for 4 to 14 days. The duration of treatment should be determined based on the severity of the infection, the location of the infection, and the patient’s clinical response. 2. The safety and efficacy of this drug have not been established in patients under 18 years of age. 3. This drug is substantially excreted by the kidneys, and patients with impaired renal function may have an increased risk of adverse reactions. Geriatric patients are more likely to have reduced renal function; therefore, dose selection should be done cautiously, and renal function should be monitored. 4. Dosage adjustments are not required based on age but should be based on renal function. Refer to adult dosing guidelines. 5. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam reduces the effectiveness of intravesical live BCG therapy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Antimicrobial therapy for other infections may interfere with the effectiveness of intravesical BCG. Antibiotics active against mycobacteria are of particular concern, but avoiding all antimicrobial therapy during BCG treatment is recommended. 6. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam reduces the effectiveness of the cholera vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration with systemic antibiotics, as they may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 7. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam decreases the serum concentration of valproic acid/divalproex sodium by an unknown mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Data suggest carbapenems may inhibit the hydrolysis of the valproic acid glucuronide metabolite back to valproic acid, leading to reduced serum concentrations. 8. Coadministration of ganciclovir with imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam may increase the risk of seizures. Avoid unless the potential benefit outweighs the risk. 9. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam reduces the effectiveness of oral microbiota therapy due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antibacterial agents may decrease the efficacy of oral microbiota therapy by interfering with bacterial spores. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating oral microbiota therapy. 10. Probenecid increases the levels of imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam by decreasing renal clearance. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Coadministration increases the plasma level and half-life of imipenem. 11. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam reduces the effectiveness of sodium picosulfate by altering metabolism. Antibiotics may decrease the efficacy of sodium picosulfate by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert it to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Imipenem/cilastatin/relebactam reduces the effectiveness of the typhoid vaccine (live) due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Postpone administering the vaccine until at least 3 days after completing the antibiotic regimen. 13. Cyclosporine may increase the neurotoxic effects of imipenem. Case reports describe imipenem increasing or decreasing cyclosporine serum concentration levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been reported in patients receiving beta-lactam therapy. Carefully assess allergy history for previous hypersensitivity to carbapenems, penicillins, cephalosporins, other beta-lactams, and other allergens. 15. Clostridium difficile-associated diarrhea (CDAD) has been reported with nearly all antibacterial agents. If CDAD is suspected or confirmed, ongoing antibacterial drug use not directed against C. difficile may need to be discontinued. 16. Prescribing antibiotics in the absence of a proven or strongly suspected bacterial infection or prophylactic indication is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of drug-resistant bacteria. 17. Data are insufficient in pregnant women to determine whether there is a drug-associated risk for major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. There is insufficient data on the presence of imipenem/cilastatin and relebactam in human milk, its effects on the breastfed child, or its effects on milk production. Relebactam is present in the milk of lactating rats. 18. The drug has low aqueous solubility. To ensure complete dissolution, inspect the solution visually for particulate matter and discoloration before administration. The solution should appear colorless to yellow; discard if discoloration or visible particles are observed. Infuse intravenously over 30 minutes.
